createdBy: cpm-c6 (peer session field report, verified in code by codex-claude-bridge-dc)
impact: `model` is a request, never a floor. A caller that asks for the `max` tier gets whatever the served provider resolves — the tier carries across failover when it maps (ISS-048), but if it is dropped, unset, or the session resumes into a provider whose default is weaker, the review still answers, at whatever tier, with a normal verdict. There is no way to say "review at this tier or fail". Gates built on the bridge therefore cannot fail closed: cpm-c6 reports rejecting two approves by hand after noticing the served model was Flash rather than Pro. Ask from that report: an explicit minimum-acceptable-tier parameter (e.g. `min_tier`) that refuses with a structured error rather than serving a weaker review, plus honouring the requested tier or erroring rather than silently answering below it. Design note: the tier ordering already exists as REVIEW_TIERS (max/balanced/fast) and `tierForModel` gives the reverse lookup, so a comparison is cheap; the decision point is the served result in withFailover/the orchestrator, after the model is resolved and before the turn. Related: ISS-050.
title: No minimum-acceptable-tier gate: a caller cannot make a review fail closed instead of answering on a weaker model
